passages.original: Idem Basan. XXI p. 262 b σοφὸς γὰρ ἦν Αἴσωπος ὁ μυθοποιός (pr. I 15), ὃς ἔφη τούς ἀνθρώπους δύο πήρας ἕκαστον φέρειν γέμειν δὲ κακῶν ἑκατέραν, ἀλλὰ τὴν μὲν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, τὴν δὲ ὄπισθεν τῶν αὐτοῦ τοῦ φέροντος καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὰ μὲν ἐξ αὑτῶν κακὰ οὐχ ὁρῶσι, τὰ δὲ ἀλλότρια πάνυ ἀκριβῶς θεῶνται secutus est Babr. 66, 4 sq.
passages.english: The same [author], Basan. XXI p. 262 b: "For Aesop the fable-maker was wise (pr. I 15), who said that human beings each carry two bags, and that each of them is full of evils, but the one in front [is full] of other people's, and the one behind of those of the bearer himself; and for this reason people do not see the evils that come from themselves, but observe those of others very precisely." Babrius followed [this], 66, 4 ff.
passages.notes: The Latin and reference matter (Idem Basan., pr. I 15, secutus est Babr. 66, 4 sq.) is editorial apparatus and has been rendered literally. 'Basan.' is presumably the title of a work by the author cited in the preceding entry, which is not supplied; the author could not be identified. The phrase 'τὰ μὲν ἐξ αὑτῶν κακὰ' is rendered 'the evils that come from themselves'; it may mean simply 'their own evils'.

passages.original: Αἴσωπος ὁ σοφός, εἶπε καὶ Λιβυστίνοις
passages.english: Aesop the wise also told [this] to the Libystinians.
passages.notes: A fragment with no context. 'Libystinians' (Λιβυστίνοις) is uncertain: it may refer to Libyans or to some particular people. The verse's source is not identified.

passages.original: Cum Tyrwhitto aliis Lachmannus (fr. 142, cf. praef. p. XI) Babrio tribuit hos versus: ταῦτα δʼ Αἴσωπος ὁ Σαρδιηνὸς εἶπεν, ὅντινʼ οἱ Δελφοί ᾄδοντα μῦθον οὐ καλῶς ἐδέξαντο ἔωσαν αὐτὸν μάλʼ ἀθέως κατὰ κρημνοῦ. 1—3 servavit Apollon. Soph. lex. Hom. p. 10, 13 s. v. ἄειδε, ubi οἱ ἀδελφοὶ cod. (corr. Tyrwh.); v. 4 Schneidewinus composuit e Suidae verbis s.
passages.english: Lachmann, with Tyrwhitt and others (fr. 142, cf. preface p. XI), attributes these verses to Babrius: "These things Aesop the Sardian said, whom the Delphians, when he sang a fable, did not receive well, [but] they pushed him, most godlessly, down a cliff." Lines 1–3 are preserved by Apollonius the Sophist, Homeric Lexicon p. 10, 13, under the entry ἄειδε, where the manuscript has οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ('the brothers'; corrected by Tyrwhitt); line 4 Schneidewin put together from the words of the Suda, s.
passages.notes: The passage is editorial Latin apparatus framing Greek verses, and is rendered as it stands. It breaks off at 's.' (sub voce), and the Suda entry is given in the context after. 'ὅντινʼ' is an evident misprint for ὅντινʼ/ὅν τινʼ. The manuscript reading οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ('the brothers') was corrected to οἱ Δελφοί ('the Delphians').

passages.original: Αἴσωπός ποτε ὁ λογοποιὸς σχολὴν ἄγων εἰς ναυπήγιον εἰσῆλθεν. τῶν δὲ ναυπηγῶν σκωπτόντων τε αὐτὸν καὶ ἐκκαλουμένων εἰς ἀπόκρισιν (e), Αἴσωπος ἔλεγε „τὸ παλαιὸν χάος τε καὶ ὕδωρ γενέσθαι, τὸν δὲ Δία νοούμενον καὶ τὸ γῆς στοιχεῖον ἀναδεῖξαι παραινέσαι αὐτῇ ὅπως ἐπὶ τρὶς ἐκροφήσῃ τὴν †θάλασσαν· κἀκείνη ἀρξαμένη τὸ μὲν πρῶτον τὰ ὄρη ἐξέφηνεν· ἐκ δευτέρου δὲ ἐκροφήσασα καὶ τὰ πεδίʼ ἀπεγύμνωσεν· εἰ δὲ δόξειεν καὶ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῇ πάντοθʼ ἐκπιεῖν τὸ ὕδωρ,ἄχρηστος ὑμῖν ἡ τέχνη γενήσεται.“
passages.english: Aesop the story-writer, once having leisure, went into a shipyard. When the shipwrights mocked him and challenged him to a reply, Aesop said: "In ancient times there came to be chaos and water, and Zeus, intending to make the element of earth appear as well, urged it to swallow down the sea three times. And she began, and the first time revealed the mountains; the second time, swallowing [again], she also laid bare the plains; and if she should decide to drink up the water entirely a third time as well, your craft will become useless."
passages.notes: The edition marks θάλασσαν ('the sea') with a crux as corrupt. '(e)' after ἀπόκρισιν appears to be an apparatus or footnote mark and has been omitted. The sense of νοούμενον ('intending, having in mind') is somewhat uncertain.
